name: Ishtar
overview: The Bible reveals Ishtar, referenced as Ashtaroth or the queen of heaven, as a false deity worshiped by surrounding nations and at times by Israel when they forsook the LORD (Judges 2:13; 10:6). God warns His people against imitating the idolatrous practices of these nations, which includes seeking after their gods and engaging in rituals that provoke His anger (Deuteronomy 12:30; Jeremiah 7:18). This idolatry stands in stark contrast to the true worship of the LORD, who alone is sovereign over all kingdoms and worthy of building His house in Jerusalem (Ezra 1:2). The fall of Lucifer, described as the morning star, also serves as a sobering reminder of the consequences of pride and rebellion against God (Isaiah 14:12).
